t.E427.agn: In 2006 EFSA found the toxicological data insufficient to set an ADI, but concluded that cassia gum meeting the newly defined purity criteria does not raise a safety concern at the proposed uses. The purity criteria include limiting anthraquinones that occur naturally in the seeds.
t.E427.body: Cassia gum is absorbed very little and is broken down in the gut.
t.E427.found.1: Milk-based desserts and flavoured fermented milk products
t.E427.found.2: Sauces, salad dressings and dehydrated soups
t.E427.prod: It is obtained by physical means from plant seeds or tree sap (gum).
t.E427.regx.0: No safety concern at the proposed uses; data insufficient to set an ADI.
t.E427.regx.1: Permitted in ice cream (2,500 mg/kg), dairy products, desserts, fillings, processed cheese, sauces, dehydrated soups and heat-treated meat products (1,500 mg/kg).
t.E427.summary: A gum obtained from the seeds of the cassia plant. It provides thickness in creams, cheese and meat products.
t.E427.what: It forms a gel and thickens.
